o.text: From Proto-Turkic *kentir, *kendir (“hemp”). Cognate with Turkish kendir.
Borrowed from Russian алкоголи́зм (alkogolízm), ultimately New Latin alcoholismus chronicus, coined by the Swedish professor of medicine Magnus Huss in 1849.
Borrowed from Arabic حُكْمًا (ḥukman), adverbial accusative of حُكْم (ḥukm). By surface analysis, hökm + -ən.
Borrowed from Arabic كَتَّان (kattān), from Classical Syriac ܟܶܬܳܢܳܐ (kettānā, “flax; linen”).
Ultimately from Middle Mongol ᠴᠢᠳᠦᠷ (čidür), whence also Khalkha Mongolian чөдөрлөх (čödörlöx).
